content:
Over the years, Apple has been adding more customisation options to iOS. iOS 16 brought back full lock screen personalisation, iOS 18 added icon colour tinting, iOS 26 introduced translucent icons, and iOS 27 brings full-screen Liquid Glass sliders.

Expanding iPhone personalisation is a good thing. Now that you can tint your home screen icons, why not extend that feature to the entire OS?

iOS 27 hasn't launched yet, so it's probably too early to think about what Apple might do in the next software version. However, I think adding theme app colours beyond just light and dark mode would be a logical next step.

Basically, I want to recreate Material You's aesthetic on iOS — but based on icon colour rather than wallpaper — though Apple should also offer a wallpaper-based option. Apple debuted the option to match icons to MagSafe case colours last year, and a theme system like this would complement that nicely.

It's worth noting that Apple already introduced colour themes to its integrated development environment, Xcode, earlier this year at WWDC. There are some great options there — why not bring that fun to the iPhone? Even on Mac, users can now set system-level colour tints for third-party apps.

Summary

Overall, I think bringing colour themes to iOS would be a great move and another big step toward giving users more customisation.

What do you think about bringing colour themes to iOS and iPadOS? Let us know in the comments.
